content:
Hello! I have been working on a simple domain theory library, and I'd like to gauge whether there is interest in incorporating it into mathlib. You can find the source code here:
https://github.com/zilberstein/domain-theory

I developed this library because some of the mathlib definitions are quite inconvenient to use. In particular, the CompletePartialOrder class has two drawbacks:

  1. It extends SupSet, which requires you to define the supremum for any set, which may not be possible if the set is not directed.
  2. lubOfDirected does not require sets to be nonempty. In general, a DCPO only needs to provide suprema for nonempty directed sets

My new library fixes both of those issues. It also follows a structure that is more similar to the existing OmegaCompletePartialOrder, and ChainCompletePartialOrder classes. That is, I defined a new type for directed sets called DSet, and the new DCPO class only requires you to define suprema of DSets.

I also proved Markowsky's theorem, which states that a poset is a DCPO iff it is Chain Complete, which I don't believe currently exists in mathlib.

Let me know if there is interest in incorporating this into mathlib, and possible deprecating CompletePartialOrder, or whether I should just keep it as a standalone library. Thanks!

Your point 1 is going against what we call junk values, see eg https://xenaproject.wordpress.com/2020/07/05/division-by-zero-in-type-theory-a-faq/ for an explanation of what I mean. Your point 2 has been discussed previously, this is a genuine mistake on mathlib's part. Please open a PR to fix it!
Probably the path of least resistance for the Directed farce is just to rename it Predirected.
The Directed farce? Is the definition of docs#DirectedOn mathematically incorrect?
directed sets have upper bounds for finite subsets, directed sets in mathlib have upper bounds for finite nonempty subsets
this matters exactly when the poset is empty, right?

Yes. But it matters a great deal in the sense that mathlib is advertised as a reliable mathematical library containing definitions as agreed upon by mathematicians, and here we disagree from the literature.

I am going to make this PR changing it to Predirected, I am sick of flagging this and I believe that it is a serious issue.

Oh yes, I totally agree! And moreover it's annoying because as I say in #mathlib4 > When should subobjects be bundled? my preorderings failed to satisfy docs#CompletePartialOrder when morally they should (because sometimes there are no preorderings on a ring, so the empty set of preorderings has no supremum...)

Was just trying to pin down what the error was because I hadn't thought about these definitions before.
Thank you, yes this was exactly my problem. Defining a CompletePartialOrder essentially requires the poset to have a bottom element, otherwise it is impossible to define a supremum for an empty set.

On the point about CompletePartialOrders, I surfaced this issue a while ago and started a PR to add nonemptiness as a constraint, but the change ended up touching so many files that I gave up. I think it would be easier to create a second typeclass, deprecate the original, and then move over to it gradually using a few commits, rather than one enormous one. What is the best practice for refactors like this?

Noam Zilberstein said:

On the point about CompletePartialOrders, I surfaced this issue a while ago and started a PR to add nonemptiness as a constraint, but the change ended up touching so many files that I gave up

My recent experience is that LLMs are very good at grinding through such menial work. Have you tried getting one of them to refactor for you?

Kevin Buzzard said:

Yes. But it matters a great deal in the sense that mathlib is advertised as a reliable mathematical library containing definitions as agreed upon by mathematicians, and here we disagree from the literature.

I am not an expert in this area, but not everybody agree on the "right" definition. Once, while I was assuming that "ensemble ordonné filtrant" (directed ordered set) implied nonempty, Gabber corrected me saying that Bourbaki did not assume nonempty, and I should write "ensemble ordonné filtrant non vide" instead.

Yaël Dillies said:

My recent experience is that LLMs are very good at grinding through such menial work. Have you tried getting one of them to refactor for you?

My last attempt was ~1 year ago and I don't think that LLMs were good enough yet, but you're right that they're probably capable now!

Joël Riou said:

Kevin Buzzard said:

Yes. But it matters a great deal in the sense that mathlib is advertised as a reliable mathematical library containing definitions as agreed upon by mathematicians, and here we disagree from the literature.

I am not an expert in this area, but not everybody agree on the "right" definition. Once, while I was assuming that "ensemble ordonné filtrant" (directed ordered set) implied nonempty, Gabber corrected me saying that Bourbaki did not assume nonempty, and I should write "ensemble ordonné filtrant non vide" instead.

I have no problem if Directed and DirectedOn remain possibly nonempty. From the perspective of domain theory, it seems strictly better if nonemptiness is required in lubOfDirected from CompletePartialOrder. Since the LUB of the empty set must be bottom, including empty sets is essentially equivalent to having an OrderBot instance, which is not always the case. So, requiring nonemptiness makes CompletePartialOrder strictly more flexible.

We could also make another type class PointedCompletePartialOrder, which also extends OrderBot, where lubOfDirected includes empty sets.
